findings.summary: `holdout integrity`'s clean line read 'N registered body/bodies, every one matching its register row and its validation manifest'. Bodies dated before MANIFEST_REQUIRED_SINCE have their manifest SKIPPED by vault_integrity_problems, not verified. On the operator's real vault — 20 bodies, all dated 2026-08-15/16, all pre-cutoff — the command printed manifest assurance for 20 bodies having checked ZERO. The register-sha half of the sentence was true; the manifest half was asserted by the wording and verified by nothing. Found on the command's FIRST real invocation, in the same session that shipped it.
findings.disposition: The clean line now separates what was verified from what was skipped: 'every one matching its register sha. Validation manifests CHECKED for k of N', plus an explicit line naming the grandfathered remainder and why it is not a bricked run. Red-first: the new test asserts '0 of 1' for a pre-cutoff body and '1 of 1' for a post-cutoff one and failed against the old wording, quoting the overclaim verbatim. This is §12's scope rule applied to a REASSURANCE rather than a finding — the direction that gets less scrutiny, because nothing looks broken.

findings.summary: Not a defect in this diff — a state finding surfaced by running the new command. The private vault holds 20 approved holdout bodies (register rows dated 2026-08-15/16), but calibration/plant-forms.md has ZERO holdout classes and `plant_forms.py check` reports the leakage tripwire UNARMED: 'scanned 29 files across 4 of 9 roots and could not have failed'. So bodies were approved into the vault without the public-side registration the tripwire reads, which means the mechanism meant to detect holdout leakage remains inert and the quarterly LIFT read stays hard-blocked. The FIRST HOLDOUT ASSIGNMENT debt on the `plant-forms` capability describes this accurately and is NOT stale; this session initially misread it as 'no vault exists' and that misreading is corrected here.
findings.disposition: Left OPEN and untouched. Paying it means deciding what the public register records for private bodies (the schema allows a `private` sha) and touching the private vault, which is David's call, not an agent's — and the existing dated debt already carries it with a Done condition ('>=1 holdout class in plant-forms.md with check reporting ARMED') and a 2026-10-15 expiry that will RED the suite. Recorded here so the gap is visible from the review trail rather than only from a debt entry that a reader can misinterpret, as happened in this session.
